record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.original_question: Does there exist a sequence of finite graphs (G_n) such that for every infection probability p>0, majority bootstrap percolation on G_n infects every vertex with probability tending to 1 as n→∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Does there exist a sequence of graphs (Gn)n∈N such that for every p > 0: limn→∞ Pp(A(Gn)) = 1 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ and a parameter $p\in(0,1)$, define the random initial set $A_0\subseteq V$ by including each vertex independently with probability $p$. The majority bootstrap percolation process on $G$ is the deterministic monotone process producing sets $A_0\subseteq A_1\subseteq A_2\subseteq\cdots$ where, for each $t\ge 0$,
$$A_{t+1}=A_t\cup\bigl\{v\in V:\ |N(v)\cap A_t|\ge \tfrac{1}{2}\deg(v)\bigr\},$$
with $N(v)$ the neighborhood of $v$. Say that the process percolates if $\bigcup_{t\ge 0}A_t=V$, and let $\mathcal{A}(G)$ denote this event. Write $\mathbb{P}_p(\mathcal{A}(G))$ for its probability under the $p$-random initial set.

Question: Does there exist a sequence $(G_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of finite graphs such that for every $p>0$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}_p\bigl(\mathcal{A}(G_n)\bigr)=1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface substantial literature on majority bootstrap percolation (hypercube, G(n,p), regular graphs, tori, permutahedron), but none of the located references explicitly affirm or refute the existence of a graph sequence for which percolation occurs with probability tending to 1 for every fixed p>0. Recent work on high-dimensional graphs (e.g., the permutahedron) studies sharp thresholds rather than this universal-p question, so the status appears unresolved from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Majority bootstrap percolation on the permutahedron and other high-dimensional graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies critical probabilities and phase transitions for majority bootstrap percolation on high-dimensional graphs including the permutahedron.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on sharp thresholds rather than constructing a sequence percolating for every fixed p>0.

status_evidence.title: Majority Bootstrap Percolation on G(n,p)
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp bounds on the critical size of the initially infected set for majority bootstrap percolation on Erdős–Rényi random graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results address thresholds on specific graph models, not the universal-p existence question.

status_evidence.title: Majority bootstrap percolation on the hypercube
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a sharp threshold for majority bootstrap percolation on the discrete hypercube.
status_evidence.claim: The hypercube has a nontrivial threshold, so it does not by itself answer the universal-p question.
